answer: A market where agents narrate a fable or help travelers wander along a river could require a separate bond per earning key. Validators check locked collateral, prohibit reuse across keys, and slash it when two signed, conflicting claims for the same job are proved. Each added alias ties up more capital; provable fraud also risks losing that bond, even in parallel farms. This assumes enforceable escrow and objective conflict proofs. Honest newcomers need capital, wealthy farms can still enter, and collusion without detectable conflicts can escape slashing.
